title: The Blockwise Alperin Weight Conjecture
main_claim: For every prime p, finite group G and p-block B, l(B)=|W_p(B)| (numerical blockwise Alperin weight conjecture). The paper reduces this, via chain inversion and a p-adic trace limit of a central detecting element E(1-c_X), to uniform p^h-divisibility of counts of generating genus-one tuples [x,y]u_1...u_n=1 (n=p^s, u_i p-singular) for groups J with O_p(J)=1. It then proves that divisibility geometrically: Galois/Sylow orbits on J-covers of a high-index marked genus-one curve over a spherically complete field K_s, together with a sharp inseparable genus bound and a specialization/connectedness argument, force a nontrivial normal p-subgroup (inertia), which contradicts O_p(J)=1.

- S5 at p=2, 3, 5, single-class and two-class multisets with p-power multiplicities

Twist (sec:twist): the index-n argument (cycle-sum rationality, the endomorphism comparison giving β_i constant and [b]P=0), index base change, and the label-rank bound dim Ω_{S/F'} ≤ h.

- deg det Ω_{C/κ} = -2χ via conormal sequence and duality
- separable different bound
- height-one Ekedahl formula det Q = (det F)^p, including the Frobenius transition matrix computed by hand
- rank of H_j = n+1-m_j
- full-divisor vanishing of the label covectors at ramified labels
- the exterior-power degree bound b_j°/d_j ≥ |S_j|-h-m_j
- the recurrence and its weights summing to 1-1/r_i
- the rounding step: both ν(Z) and d·Σ(1-1/r_i) are degrees of divisors over F, hence multiples of p^{s-h}
- sanity case: Frobenius-type covers are unramified at the independent labels, consistent with the bound

Specialization:
- Gauss valuation and section reduction
- Σ m_w = m and m_w = |Δ_w|
- d = |I_w| is a p-power
- the inequality chain giving Σ(|q_i-b_i| + δ_i q_i) ≤ 0, re-derived
- Veronese finite-presentation model
- Noetherian normal approximation and Stein connectedness

Valuations: mixed lift, orthogonal bases over a spherically complete field, defectless full residue degree, simultaneous approximation, Galois invariance of the tuple classes using roots of unity in K_s, the Sylow splitting of the Z(J)-extension (p ∤ |Z(J)|), and residue permutations.

Not fully verified: the existence construction of the maximal immediate extension K_s (pages roughly 200-330 of valuations.tex, read quickly), and the Stacks-cited foundations, which were taken as given.
